statements: Finance wants to download the orders as a CSV file they can open in Excel. Add GET /orders/export.csv, which sends that file.
The file starts with a header row, then has one row per order, with these columns in this order and exactly these header names: id, created_at, customer, status, total, currency.

The export contains every order that matches the filters, however many there are. It is one file, not pages: the paging options of the order list do not apply to it. Rows come in the same order as in the order list.
The export understands the same filters as the order list (status, from, to), with exactly the same meaning. A filter value the list would refuse is refused the same way.

total is shown as a decimal amount with two decimal places (for example 19.99), also for refunds, and never as a number of cents. id, created_at, status and currency show the same values the JSON API shows.
The file must open correctly in Excel, and every cell must show what the data says, whatever a customer typed as their name.
The browser saves the response as a file, named after the day of the export (for example orders-2025-03-14.csv).
A search with no matching orders still gives a valid file.
Everything that exists today keeps working exactly as it does now.
The README documents the new endpoint.
The new behaviour has tests in test/. Keep the change focused on what this ticket needs.
brief: Add GET /orders/export.csv to the orders service as the numbered ticket statements describe, document it in the README and add tests under test/. Follow the conventions already in the code. Change only what the ticket needs.
